posts.title: Morning forecast for Vallecito, Bayfield and Durango
posts.body:
09/11/26 5:04am: Friday morning, and theres still not a drop on the woodpile. Dry is the whole story for the county today.

The bus run should be straightforward this morning. Durango and the Animas Valley start in the upper 50s and climb to the mid-80s this afternoon. Bayfield and up the Pine start low 50s and track the same pattern. Vallecito and the Florida start mid-50s, then push into the low 80s by afternoon.

All the models agree we stay dry through the day. The Euro, GFS, ICON and GEM all show zero precipitation through tonight and tomorrow, so theres no disagreement to hedge. A few afternoon clouds maybe, but nothing that develops.

Wind picks up this afternoon, gusts to 20-25mph in town and Bayfield, a bit less up the Florida. The high Weminuche stays breezy through the day, gusts 15-25 up there.

The 550 north should stay dry over Coal Bank, Molas and Red Mountain through the day. I'd expect Wolf Creek on the 160 to run the same. That's the forecast, not the road status, so check CDOT for current conditions and chain law: https://www.cotrip.org/

Districts decide by 6:30 as usual and I'd expect a clean drive in this morning.

Vallecito's still sitting at 22% of full pool and the SNOTEL up there is showing 0.1" SWE with 3" of depth, which is just trace stuff from whatever blew through earlier this week.

The Grand Junction discussion is watching SubTrop moisture trying to work north into the Four Corners this weekend, so things could get more interesting Saturday and Sunday, but today stays quiet.

I'll have more later if anything changes.

posts.title: Morning forecast for Vallecito, Bayfield and Durango
posts.body:
09/10/26 5:06am: Second morning running I havent had to wipe the windshield, and that tells you most of what today holds.

Durango and the Animas Valley should see a straightforward morning, then a warm afternoon pushing near 90 under sun. Light winds early, gusts 15-25 this afternoon. Tomorrow looks similar, just a tick cooler with a slim rain chance late in the day that I dont think amounts to much.

Bayfield and up the Pine, same setup. Clear start, warming through the 80s, breezy this afternoon with gusts 18-28. Tomorrow stays dry through the school run, with that same low-end pop showing up in the models for late afternoon Friday.

Vallecito and up the Florida, youre looking at mid-50s this morning and low 80s this afternoon. Winds lighter than down valley, 10-19mph gusts. Tomorrow morning stays clear for the early drive, with Friday afternoon showing a sliver of a rain chance that all four models agree is basically nothing.

The high Weminuche sits in the upper 40s this morning and climbs to near 70 this afternoon. Breezy up top both days, gusts 20-30 Friday afternoon.

The passes should stay dry through today and tomorrow morning. Coal Bank, Molas and Red Mountain should all be clear for the early runs, and I'd expect Wolf Creek to be the same. For current road status and chain law: https://www.cotrip.org/

The SNOTEL at Vallecito is sitting at 0.1" SWE and 4" depth, which is trace stuff from earlier in the week. The Animas at Durango is running 153 cfs.

The Grand Junction discussion has us under building high pressure with zonal flow keeping things dry through Friday. They're watching a moisture push for the weekend, but theres disagreement on timing and whether any frontal boundary holds together enough to actually fire anything. The ECENS is later and weaker than the GEFS, and the forcing question is still open. More on that tomorrow as it tightens up.

Anybody else already thinking about when this heat breaks?

posts.title: Morning forecast for Vallecito, Bayfield and Durango
posts.body:
09/09/26 5:09am: The gauge stayed dry overnight and the morning drive down the 501 should be straightforward.

Districts decide by 6:30 as always, but there's nothing in the weather to slow anybody down this morning. Durango and Bayfield both start cool (mid-50s to near 60F) and warm fast into the low-to-mid 80s this afternoon. Clear all day, light winds early, picking up a bit this afternoon but nothing that'll cause trouble.

Up the Pine and around Vallecito we're starting in the upper 50s and topping out low 80s. Same deal, dry through the day. Pop values tick up a hair late afternoon but that's just the models acknowledging September exists, not a real chance at anything.

The high country woke up around 50F and gets into the upper 60s today. Still dry up there, winds picking up a bit through the afternoon (gusts to 18-19mph) but nothing dramatic.

The passes should stay dry all day. Coal Bank, Molas and Red Mountain get light winds early, a bit gustier this afternoon, but no weather. Wolf Creek the same. For current road status check https://www.cotrip.org/ before you head out.

All four models (Euro, GFS, ICON, GEM) agree we stay bone dry through tomorrow, and GJ's discussion has us staying that way through Thursday. They're watching Friday for a possible moisture push depending on how a trough off the Pacific Northwest tracks, but that's still days out and the setup's uncertain.

The Vallecito SNOTEL's still showing that trace from last week (0.1" SWE, 3" depth) but everything else is at zero. Animas at Durango running 165 cfs, Los Pinos above the lake at 26 cfs.

What's the morning looking like at your place?
